areas.name: Left console
areas.text: The panel to the pilot's left with the engine start switches, the fuel panel, the power lever, the flap lever, the emergency controls and the circuit breakers.

panels.name: Engine control panel (start switches)
panels.text: This panel on the left console starts the jet engine. It has the start and ignition switches, a switch for outside power, a computer button and an anti-ice button.
panels.context: The manual says every cockpit has such a panel, but the engine can be started only from the front cockpit. After the start the engine runs by itself.

controls.name: Engine control switches, anti-ice and GPU (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole group of engine start switches on the left console. Its parts are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The manual says the starter switches itself off at 50 percent N2 (core speed), when the engine can run by itself.

controls.name: STARTER MODE selector (NORMAL, CRANK)

positions.name: Normal
positions.text: The automatic start sequence is ready. The engine starts when the ignition switch is held to START.

positions.name: Crank
positions.text: The engine is only turned by the starter, with no start sequence. This clears fuel left in the combustion chamber.

controls.text: This switch chooses between a normal engine start and only spinning the engine without fuel. Spinning without fuel clears left-over fuel after a failed start.
controls.context: The manual calls it the START switch, marked NORMAL and VENTILACION (CRANK).

controls.name: CONTINUOUS IGNITION/START switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The igniters are off.

positions.name: START
positions.text: The igniters and the starter-generator are energised (hold for about 2 seconds).

positions.name: CONTINUOUS
positions.text: Only the igniters are on, to keep the engine lit.

controls.text: This switch lights the engine. Holding it to START for about 2 seconds starts the igniters and the starter. In CONT IGN only the igniters run, as a safety against the engine going out.
controls.context: The manual says to use continuous ignition for take-off, landing, icing, heavy turbulence and thunderstorms. The yellow ignition light is on while the igniters work.

controls.name: ENGINE START (ignition) light test
controls.text: This yellow light shows when the igniters are on. Pressing it tests the bulb.
controls.context: The manual calls it the ignition light, a press-to-test light next to the ignition switch.

controls.name: ABORT start switch

positions.name: NEUTRAL
positions.text: The start continues normally.

positions.name: ABORT
positions.text: The starter-generator is switched off while the switch is held.

controls.text: Holding this switch to ABORT switches the starter off, to stop a start that goes wrong. It springs back when released.
controls.context: The manual says it is used before the starter drops out by itself at 50 percent N2. It is also used for a start with the engine computer out of order.

controls.name: COMPUTER button (engine computer)
controls.text: This lamp-button switches the engine computer between automatic mode (the light stays out) and manual mode (MAN lights amber). The engine computer helps look after the fuel supply of the engine.
controls.context: If the computer fails, an amber COMPUT. light comes on in the warning panel.

controls.name: ANTI-ICE button (engine)
controls.text: This lamp-button turns the engine anti-ice on. Warm air from the engine then keeps ice from forming at the engine inlet. ON shows when it is working.
controls.context: The manual says ice can form when the air is at or below 10 degrees Celsius and there is visible moisture.

controls.name: GPU (ground power) button
controls.text: This lamp-button connects an outside power cart (GPU) to the plane's electrical system. GPU shows green when a cart is plugged in and ready, and ON shows when its power is connected.
controls.context: The manual says the batteries and the generator disconnect by themselves while the outside power is connected.

panels.name: Fuel control panel
panels.text: This panel on the left console controls how fuel moves from the wing tanks to the main tank and shows how much fuel is left.
panels.context: The plane has four tanks: one in the fuselage, one in the centre wing and one in each outer wing. The engine always draws from the fuselage tank. The wing tanks feed it through pumps.

controls.name: Fuel panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole fuel panel of the left console. Its pump switches, valve switch and quantity controls are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The manual says the fuel quantity is measured only in the fuselage and centre tanks, and not in the outer wing tanks.

controls.name: Fuel transfer pump switch, left

positions.name: AUT
positions.text: The pump runs until all the fuel of this tank has been moved.

positions.name: MAN
positions.text: The pump runs until the switch is set to OFF. The manual says to use this only in abnormal cases, so the pump does not run dry.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The pump is off.

controls.text: This switch controls the transfer pump of the left outer wing tank. The pump moves fuel from that tank into the fuselage tank.
controls.context: The manual says to use up the outer wing tanks first, then the centre tank.

controls.name: Fuel transfer pump switch, centre 1

positions.name: AUT
positions.text: The pump runs until all the fuel of this tank has been moved.

positions.name: MAN
positions.text: The pump runs until the switch is set to OFF.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The pump is off.

controls.text: This switch controls the first of two transfer pumps in the centre wing tank.
controls.context: The centre tank has two pumps. Together with the left and right outer tank pumps there are four transfer pumps.

controls.name: Fuel transfer pump switch, centre 2

positions.name: AUT
positions.text: The pump runs until all the fuel of this tank has been moved.

positions.name: MAN
positions.text: The pump runs until the switch is set to OFF.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The pump is off.

controls.text: This switch controls the second transfer pump in the centre wing tank.
controls.context: A second pump in the same tank keeps fuel moving if the first one fails.

controls.name: Fuel transfer pump switch, right

positions.name: AUT
positions.text: The pump runs until all the fuel of this tank has been moved.

positions.name: MAN
positions.text: The pump runs until the switch is set to OFF.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The pump is off.

controls.text: This switch controls the transfer pump of the right outer wing tank.
controls.context: It works like the left switch. Check valves stop fuel from flowing from one wing tank to another.

controls.name: Fuselage tank pump (boost pump) switch
controls.text: This guarded lamp-button controls the boost pump, a pump in the fuselage tank that pushes fuel to the engine. The button is dark while the pump works. Pressing it stops the pump and OFF lights up. A cover protects the button.
controls.context: The manual says the pump is submerged in the engine feed cell of the fuselage tank.

controls.name: Engine fuel valve (shut-off) switch
controls.text: This guarded lamp-button controls the shut-off valve between the fuselage tank and the engine. OFF lights up when the valve is closed. A cover protects the button.
controls.context: An amber FUEL VALVE light on the warning panel comes on whenever the valve is not fully open.

controls.name: Fuel quantity selector (centre wing tank quantity)
controls.text: This lamp-button chooses what the fuel quantity dial shows: only the fuselage tank (FUS lights amber) or the fuselage tank plus the centre wing tank.
controls.context: The manual says that without transfer pressure the dial always shows the fuselage tank only.

controls.name: Test fuel quantity indicator button
controls.text: While this button is held, the fuel quantity dial shows the fuselage and centre tank contents added together.
controls.context: The manual says this test button is found in the front cockpit only. The outer wing tanks can only be estimated from the fuel used counter.

panels.name: Power lever quadrant, flap lever and gear warning silence
panels.text: The power lever, the flap lever and a silence button are mounted together on the left console. The power lever works the engine, the flap lever the flaps.
panels.context: The manual says the front power lever has a friction lock. Both cockpits have a lever, joined by a flexible link.

controls.name: Power lever idle/stop gate (THROTTLE IDLE DETENT)

positions.name: Idle
positions.text: The power lever is at idle.

positions.name: Stop
positions.text: The power lever is at STOP and the fuel is cut off.

controls.text: This is the gate at the idle end of the power lever travel. The pilot lifts the lever to pass the gate from IDLE to STOP. At STOP the fuel to the engine is cut.
controls.context: The gate protects against shutting the fuel off by accident while slowing down. The game offers the positions Idle, Stop and a two-position idle/stop switch.

controls.name: Power lever friction knob (THROTTLE FRICTION)
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the power lever stiffer or looser, so it stays where the pilot puts it.
controls.context: The manual says only the front power lever has a friction lock.

controls.name: Landing gear warning silence button
controls.text: Pressing this button silences the warning tone that sounds when the wheels are up and the engine power is low.
controls.context: The manual says the tone sounds when a wheel is not down and locked below 6500 feet and 75 percent N1. The amber GEAR light stays on as long as this is true.

controls.name: Flap lever (FLAP POSITION SELECTOR)

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The flaps are fully retracted.

positions.name: TAKEOFF
positions.text: The flaps are set to 10 degrees.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The flaps are set to 30 degrees.

controls.text: This lever sets the flaps, the parts of the wing that slide out to give more lift at low speed. It has three marked positions: UP, TAKEOFF (10 degrees) and DOWN (30 degrees).
controls.context: The pilot sets TAKEOFF for take-off and DOWN for landing. The three windows on the instrument panel show where the flaps are.

panels.name: Emergency panel (left console)
panels.text: This panel holds backup controls for failures of the trim, the speed brake and the ailerons, plus the emergency landing gear handle and the seat height switch.
panels.context: These controls are normally left alone. Several have guards or covers so they cannot be moved by accident.

controls.name: Emergency flight control panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the emergency panel with its trim switch, speed brake button, aileron cutout and test light. Each part is explained below.
controls.context: The manual shows seven parts in its picture: emergency elevator trim switch, servo-actuator cutout switch, emergency speed brake switch, seat elevation switch, press-to-test light, trim tone breaker and thermal breaker.

controls.name: Emergency elevator trim switch (with guard)

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The pitch trim moves to nose up.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: No emergency trim. The trim works from the stick switch.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The pitch trim moves to nose down.

controls.text: This switch trims the nose up or down if the trim switch on the stick fails. A guard must be turned aside first. Trim means a steady push that keeps the plane flying straight without holding the stick.
controls.context: The manual says that with the guard open the trim switches on the stick and the speed brake are cut out.

controls.name: PITCH TRIM DISC lamp test
controls.text: This light comes on when the emergency trim switch drives the stabilizer. Pressing it tests the bulb.
controls.context: The manual calls it the press-to-test light next to the emergency trim switch.

controls.name: Pitch trim breaker (thermal breaker)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The emergency trim circuit has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The emergency trim circuit is cut off.

controls.text: This is the thermal breaker that protects the emergency trim. It pops out and cuts the power if the trim motor takes too much current.
controls.context: The manual says this breaker is found only in the front cockpit.

controls.name: Pitch trim tone mute breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The trim tone sounds as normal.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The trim tone is muted.

controls.text: While the trim moves, a warning tone sounds in the headset. This breaker mutes that tone.
controls.context: The manual says that pulling the TRIM TONE breaker silences the tone and then the guards no longer cut out the trim and airbrake.

controls.name: EMERGENCY AIR BRAKE RETRACT button
controls.text: Pressing this guarded button lets the speed brake close partly if the hydraulics fail, because the wind then pushes it in.
controls.context: The manual says this reduces the large drag that the fully open brake makes.

controls.name: AILERON HYD OVERRIDE (servo-actuator cutout) with cover
controls.text: This guarded button cuts the hydraulic help from the ailerons, so a pilot can practise flying with heavy controls. MAN lights when it is on.
controls.context: The manual says this function is not simulated in DCS: C-101.

controls.name: SEAT HEIGHT ADJUSTMENT switch
controls.text: This switch moves the ejection seat up or down, to suit the pilot's height.
controls.context: The manual says the seat elevation switch has two positions, UP and DOWN, that show the direction of travel.

controls.name: EMERGENCY LANDING GEAR EXTENSION handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle lowers the wheels with a bottle of nitrogen gas if the normal system fails. It works whatever position the gear handle is in.
controls.context: The manual says it can be used only once. After the gear has been lowered this way, it cannot be raised by hydraulics again. The label is EMERG. TREN.

panels.name: Seat harness handle and canopy safety catch
panels.text: These two controls are at the left side of the seat: the shoulder harness handle and the catch that secures the canopy.
panels.context: They are used when strapping in and when opening or closing the canopy.

controls.name: SHOULDER HARNESS CONTROL HANDLE
controls.text: The game names this handle 'SHOULDER HARNESS CONTROL HANDLE'. The manual does not describe it. A shoulder harness is the belt that holds the pilot in the seat.
controls.context: It is one of the seat controls of the game's cockpit.

controls.name: Canopy safety catch
controls.text: Squeezing this catch lets the pilot open the canopy. To close and lock it, the pilot grabs the catch first, closes the canopy and then moves the locking handle forward.
controls.context: The manual describes the canopy opening to the right.

panels.name: Circuit breaker panel, part 1 (front left console)
panels.text: These circuit breakers are small push-in safety switches. Each one protects one electrical circuit and pops out when too much current flows.
panels.context: The manual says most electrical circuits are protected by pop-out thermal breakers. The main panel is on the front left console and a secondary panel on the rear left console covers circuits of the rear cockpit only.

controls.text: This is the whole circuit breaker panel on the front left console. It holds a row of small push-in safety switches, one for each electrical circuit.

areas.name: Right console
areas.text: The panel to the pilot's right with the lights, the audio panel, the radios, the air conditioning and the oxygen controls.

panels.name: Illumination panel (cockpit and outside lights)
panels.text: This panel on the right console switches the lights: the cockpit lights for night flying and the lights on the outside of the plane.
panels.context: The manual says the cockpit lights are controlled in each cockpit, while the outside lights are controlled from the front cockpit only. The rear cockpit has its own lamps for the cabin.

controls.name: Illumination panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole light panel on the right console. Its knobs and switches are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The manual lists seven controls: console lights, integral instrument light, anti-collision light, formation lights, position lights, auxiliary lights and storm lights.

controls.name: INSTRUMENT LIGHTING knob
controls.text: Turning this knob switches on the lights inside the instruments and sets how bright they are.
controls.context: The manual calls it the integral instrument light switch.

controls.name: CONSOLE INTEGRAL LIGHTING knob
controls.text: Turning this knob switches on the lights of the console panels (the side panels) and sets their brightness.
controls.context: The manual calls it the console lights switch.

controls.name: STORM LIGHTS switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The storm lights are on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The storm lights are off.

controls.text: This switch turns on the storm lights. These are very bright white lights that light the whole cockpit, so lightning flashes do not blind the pilot.
controls.context: The manual says there are two storm lights in each cockpit.

controls.name: RED FLOOD LIGHTING switch (auxiliary lights)

positions.name: BRIGHT
positions.text: The lights are on at full brightness. The manual calls this BRILLO.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The lights are off.

positions.name: TENUE
positions.text: The lights are on but dimmed. The manual calls this TENUE (DIM).

controls.text: This switch turns on the red auxiliary lights that gently light the cockpit at night, with two levels of brightness.
controls.context: The manual says the red auxiliary lights have the positions BRILLO (bright), OFF and TENUE (dim). Red light keeps the eyes used to the dark.

controls.name: ANTI-COLLISION BEACON switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The anti-collision light is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The anti-collision light is off.

controls.text: This switch turns on the flashing anti-collision light on the tail fin, so other aircraft can see the plane.
controls.context: The manual says the light is on the upper vertical stabilizer.

controls.name: FORMATION LIGHTS switch

positions.name: BRIGHT
positions.text: The lights are on at full brightness. The manual calls this BRILLO.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The lights are off.

positions.name: TENUE
positions.text: The lights are on but dimmed. The manual calls this TENUE (DIM).

controls.text: This switch turns on the formation lights, soft glowing strips that help pilots fly close together at night. It has two levels of brightness.
controls.context: The manual says they are controlled in the front cockpit.

controls.name: NAV LIGHTS (position lights) switch

positions.name: BRIGHT
positions.text: The lights are on at full brightness. The manual calls this BRILLO.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The lights are off.

positions.name: TENUE
positions.text: The lights are on but dimmed. The manual calls this TENUE (DIM).

controls.text: This switch turns on the position lights: red on the left wing tip, green on the right wing tip and white at the tail. It has two levels of brightness.
controls.context: The manual says the position lights also include white silhouette lights on both sides of the fuselage.

panels.name: Audio control panel (INT)
panels.text: This panel is the volume and radio mixer for the pilot's headset. It switches on the radios the pilot wants to hear and sets how loud each one is. It also controls the intercom between the two crew members.
panels.context: The manual calls it the audio control system AN/AIC-18. It lets each pilot listen to any navigation station and to any radio on his own.

controls.name: Audio panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole audio panel on the right console. Its buttons and knobs are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The panel has one button for each radio and navigation receiver, a selector switch, a general volume knob and a call button.

controls.name: Receiver on/volume buttons (UHF, VHF, TCN, VOR, MK)
controls.text: Each of these five buttons switches one receiver into the headset and sets its volume. Pulling the button out turns the receiver on. Turning it sets the volume.
controls.context: UHF and VHF are the two radios, TCN is TACAN, VOR is the VOR receiver and MK is the marker beacon receiver. Pulling out the TACAN or VOR button lets the pilot hear the station's identification tone.

controls.name: INT button (interphone on/volume)
controls.text: Pulling this button out and turning it sets the volume of the interphone, the intercom between the two crew members.
controls.context: To talk on the interphone, the pilot also sets the selector switch to INT and presses the push-to-talk switch.

controls.name: HM button (hot mic mode on/volume)
controls.text: Pulling this button out switches on the hot microphone mode. In this mode the crew can talk to each other without pressing a button.
controls.context: The manual says the HOT MIC TALK button has to be pulled out too, and this button is then turned to the volume wanted.

controls.name: HOT MIC TALK button
controls.text: Pulling this button out switches the microphone on for the hot microphone mode.
controls.context: The game labels it '(HOT MIC) TALK CIRCUIT BREAKER'. The manual calls it the HOT MIC TALK button.

controls.name: General volume knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the overall volume in the headset.
controls.context: The manual calls it the general volume knob, number 11 of the audio panel.

controls.name: Selector switch
controls.text: This switch chooses which system the pilot talks to when pressing the push-to-talk switch: for example the interphone (INT) or one of the radios.
controls.context: The manual says the selector must be at INT for talking on the interphone.

controls.name: CALL button
controls.text: Pressing this button is an emergency call between the two cockpits. It overrides the interphone and hot microphone modes.
controls.context: The manual calls it an emergency mode.

panels.name: VHF radio AN/ARC-134 control panel
panels.text: This is the control box of the VHF radio, the second radio of the plane. It sets the frequency and the volume.
panels.context: The manual says the radio covers 116.000 to 149.975 MHz in steps of 25 kHz. Both cockpits have a panel, and only one has control at a time.

controls.name: VHF comm radio panel (whole box)
controls.text: This is the whole VHF radio control box on the right console. Its switches and knobs are explained below.
controls.context: The radio is energised by the essential DC bus.

controls.name: POWER switch (VHF)
controls.text: This switch is the power switch of the VHF radio. It turns the radio on or off.
controls.context: The manual lists a power switch, number 1 in its figure. The game does not list the positions.

controls.name: DISPLAY TEST button (VHF)
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the number display of the VHF radio.
controls.context: The manual calls it the digits test.

controls.name: Frequency selector knobs (4)
controls.text: These four knobs set the frequency digit by digit: 10 MHz, 1 MHz, 0.1 MHz and 25 kHz steps. The number shows on the display.
controls.context: The frequency is the 'station number' of the radio. Both people must tune the same number to hear each other.

controls.name: VHF volume and brightness knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the display brightness and the radio volume.
controls.context: The manual calls it the dimmer/volume knob.

panels.name: VOR/ILS radio AN/ARN-127 control panel
panels.text: This is the control box of the VOR and ILS receiver. It tunes the radio beacons (VOR) and the runway beams (ILS) that guide the plane. A small test and dimmer panel sits next to it.
panels.context: The manual says the receiver covers 108.00 to 117.95 MHz in 50 kHz steps. It also receives the marker beacons. The signal shows on the HSI, ADI and RMI.

controls.name: VOR radio panel (whole box)
controls.text: This is the whole VOR/ILS control box on the right console. Its knobs and buttons are explained below.
controls.context: The manual says the panel which has gained control by the NAV transfer switch tunes the receiver.

controls.name: VOR frequency selector knobs (3)
controls.text: These three knobs tune the VOR frequency: the first in 1 MHz steps (108 to 117), the second in 0.1 MHz steps and the third in 50 kHz steps.
controls.context: A VOR is a ground beacon that tells the pilot the direction to it. The pilot reads the direction on the RMI and the HSI.

controls.name: NAV VOL knob (VOR off/volume)
controls.text: Turning this knob switches the VOR receiver on and sets its volume.
controls.context: The manual calls it the OFF/VOLUME knob.

controls.name: TEST VOR/MKR button
controls.text: Pressing this button runs the VOR test, and the three marker beacon lamps light up.
controls.context: The manual calls it the VOR/MARKERS TEST button.

controls.name: TEST VHF NAV DIGITS button
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the number display of the VOR panel.
controls.context: The manual calls it the digits test.

controls.name: DIMMER knob (VOR)
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the display of the VOR panel brighter or darker.
controls.context: It helps reading the display at night.

panels.name: TACAN AN/ARN-118 control panel
panels.text: This is the control box of the TACAN radio. TACAN tells the pilot the direction and distance to a ground or ship station that the pilot has tuned in.
panels.context: The bearing shows on the RMI and the HSI, and the distance on the HSI. The manual says each cockpit has a panel.

controls.name: TACAN radio panel (whole box)
controls.text: This is the whole TACAN control box on the right console. Its parts are explained below.
controls.context: TACAN stands for tactical air navigation. It is used by military aircraft and ships.

controls.name: TACAN channel selector (tens)
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the tens digit of the TACAN channel (00x to 12x).
controls.context: The channel is the station's 'number'. The game says: rotate the mouse wheel to select.

controls.name: TACAN channel selector (units) and X/Y mode
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the last digit of the TACAN channel. A right mouse click chooses the X or Y mode, which means the two families of channels.
controls.context: Each channel exists in an X and a Y version. The pilot must pick the one the station uses.

controls.name: TACAN mode selector

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: TACAN is off.

positions.name: REC
positions.text: The set only receives and gives bearing to the station.

positions.name: T/R
positions.text: The set transmits and receives and gives bearing and distance.

positions.name: A/A REC
positions.text: Bearing from another aircraft.

positions.name: A/A T/R
positions.text: Bearing and distance from another aircraft.

controls.text: This selector switches TACAN off or chooses what it does: receive only, receive and answer, or the same with another aircraft instead of a ground station.
controls.context: T/R also gives the distance. A/A modes work with another aircraft that has TACAN, and the channels differ by 63.

controls.name: TACAN volume knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the volume of the TACAN station's identification tone.
controls.context: The audio panel's TCN button also has to be pulled out to hear it.

controls.name: TACAN TEST button
controls.text: Pressing this button runs a self-test of the TACAN set.
controls.context: The manual lists a test button in the TACAN panel figure.

panels.name: Air conditioning and pressurization panel
panels.text: This panel controls the air in the cockpit: pressure, temperature, fresh air and the air for the windshield.
panels.context: The manual says the system uses hot air taken from the engine and cools it with air from outside. Without pressure the thin air at high altitude would be hard to breathe.

controls.name: Pressurization and environmental control panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole air conditioning panel. Its switches are explained below.
controls.context: The manual lists six controls: mode selector, temperature selector, manual control switch, emergency ventilation switch, flow selector and the air conditioning/pressurization switch.

controls.name: AIR-CONDITIONING master switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: No air conditioning or pressurization.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: Air conditioning and pressurization work.

positions.name: RESET
positions.text: The system is reset. The game names this position RESET.

controls.text: This switch turns the air conditioning and pressurization on. It must be ON for the cockpit to be pressurized and conditioned.
controls.context: The manual says the cockpit is held at a set pressure program as the plane climbs, and a red CKPT PRESS light comes on at a cabin altitude of 25000 feet.

controls.name: TEMPERATURE MODE switch (AUTO or manual)

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The temperature selector sets the temperature.

positions.name: Manual
positions.text: The manual control switch sets the temperature.

controls.text: This switch chooses how the cockpit temperature is controlled: automatically with the temperature knob, or by hand with the HOT/COLD switch.
controls.context: In AUTO the pilot sets a wanted temperature and the system holds it.

controls.name: TEMPERATURE REGULATION control knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the wanted cockpit temperature in automatic mode.
controls.context: The manual calls it the temperature selector (AUTO mode).

controls.name: MANUAL TEMPERATURE CONTROL switch (COLD, WARM)
controls.text: In manual mode, setting this switch to WARM makes the cockpit air warmer, and setting it to COLD makes it cooler.
controls.context: The manual marks the two positions CALOR (hot) and FRIO (cold). The game offers the commands COLD and WARM.

controls.name: AIR FLOW MODE switch (COCKPIT, WINDSHIELD)

positions.name: COCKPIT
positions.text: Most air flows to the cockpit.

positions.name: WINDSHIELD
positions.text: Most air flows to the de-misting outlets on the windshield and canopy.

controls.text: This switch chooses where most of the air goes: into the cockpit, or on the windshield and canopy to clear mist.
controls.context: The manual marks the positions CAB and CRISTAL (windshield). Misting means a thin layer of water on the glass.

controls.name: EMERGENCY VENTILATION switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The emergency ventilation valves are closed.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: Outside air enters the cockpit.

controls.text: This switch lets outside air flow into the cockpit through an intake on the nose, if the pressurization fails or the temperature cannot be controlled.
controls.context: The emergency valves stay closed in normal flight.

panels.name: Oxygen panel and valve lever
panels.text: This part of the right console holds the controls and gauges for the pilot's breathing oxygen.
panels.context: At high altitude the air is too thin to breathe, so the pilot breathes oxygen from two bottles in the nose of the plane.

controls.name: Oxygen system pressure gauge
controls.text: This gauge shows how much pressure is left in the oxygen bottles.
controls.context: The pressure shows on the front gauge and is repeated on the rear one. A red OXY PRESS light comes on when pressure to the regulator drops below 45 psi.

controls.name: Cabin altimeter
controls.text: This gauge shows the altitude that the air pressure inside the cockpit corresponds to. It works like a normal altimeter.
controls.context: In a pressurized cabin this is lower than the real altitude. The manual says the red CKPT PRESS light comes on at 25000 feet.

controls.name: OXYGEN SUPPLY valve lever

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The oxygen valve is open.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The oxygen valve is closed.

controls.text: This lever opens or closes the oxygen valve of this cockpit.
controls.context: The lever is marked A (open) and C (close). The pilot opens it before flight.

panels.name: Other right console controls
panels.text: These are the remaining controls on the right side of the cockpit: the canopy detachment handle and the storage box.
panels.context: None of them is used in a normal flight.

controls.name: Oxygen regulator control (100% or AIRMIX)

positions.text: The pilot breathes pure oxygen.

positions.name: AIRMIX
positions.text: Oxygen is mixed with cabin air.

controls.text: This control on the seat sets what the pilot breathes: 100% means pure oxygen, AIRMIX means oxygen mixed with cabin air.
controls.context: The game names it 'Oxygen Regulator - 100%/AIRMIX'. The manual does not describe the regulator control itself.

controls.name: CANOPY EMERGENCY JETTISON handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle lets the canopy come completely off for an emergency exit or for maintenance.
controls.context: The manual calls it the interior canopy detachment handle and says there is one on the right side of each cockpit.

controls.name: STORAGE BOX COVER
controls.text: The game names this control 'STORAGE BOX COVER'. It opens the cover of a storage box. The manual only mentions a map case on the right console.
controls.context: It is a clickable part of the game's cockpit.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: canopy hood
areas.text: The blackout hood over the rear canopy, used for instrument flight training.

panels.name: Instrument flight hood (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The hood is a set of curtains that can be pulled over the rear canopy so the student sees only the instruments.
panels.context: The instructor in the front cockpit watches the student, who sits under the hood. The manual lists it as miscellaneous equipment.

controls.name: Close/open IFR hood

positions.name: CLOSED
positions.text: The curtains are closed and block the outside view.

positions.name: OPEN
positions.text: The curtains are open and the outside view is free.

controls.text: This control closes or opens the blackout curtains over the rear canopy. With the hood closed the student cannot see outside and must fly by instruments.
controls.context: The manual calls them the instrument flight training blackout curtains, an option for the rear cockpit.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: instrument panel
areas.text: The instrument panel of the rear cockpit. It has the same dials as the front panel, and the radios, so the instructor can see and do the same.

panels.name: Flight instruments (main panel) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These are the round dials in the middle of the panel that tell the pilot how fast the plane flies, how high it is, which way it points and whether it is level.
panels.context: The pilot scans these dials all the time during flight. The rear cockpit has its own copy of the same dials, so the instructor sees the same picture. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: ADI pitch adjustment knob
controls.text: Turning this knob moves the horizontal steering bar of the ADI up or down. This sets the nose angle that the flight director should hold.
controls.context: It is used together with the PAT button of the flight director, which holds the nose angle chosen with this knob.

controls.name: ATTITUDE TEST button
controls.text: While this button is held, the ADI ball swings to a test picture: 20 degrees of roll to the right and 10 degrees nose up. This shows that the ADI works.
controls.context: The pilot uses it as a quick check of the instrument before flight.

controls.name: Altimeter baro adjust knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the air pressure number in the small window of the altimeter. Without the right number the altimeter reads too high or too low.
controls.context: The pilot sets it to the pressure the tower gives for the local airfield. The manual says the window works between 950 and 1050 millibar.

controls.name: Tap Glass button
controls.text: The game names this button 'Tap Glass'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: It appears in the game's list of clickable cockpit parts without any further description.

controls.name: Clock winding and setting knob

positions.name: PUSH
positions.text: The knob is in: turning it winds the clock.

positions.name: PULL
positions.text: The knob is out: turning it moves the clock hands to set the time.

controls.text: Turning this knob winds the clock. Pulling it out lets the pilot set the clock hands.
controls.context: The game offers the two actions as PULL and PUSH of the knob.

controls.name: CHRONOGRAPH button
controls.text: This button starts, stops and resets the stopwatch of the clock. The manual says it is a knob in the upper right corner of the clock.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to time any part of the flight.

controls.name: Airspeed bug knob
controls.text: Turning this knob moves a small triangle around the rim of the airspeed dial. The pilot puts it on a speed to remember.
controls.context: The game offers two commands for it: bug increase and bug decrease.

controls.name: G meter reset button
controls.text: Pressing this button moves the two memory pointers of the G meter back to the 1 G mark.
controls.context: The pilot presses it before a new exercise so the memory pointers start clean. The manual calls it the PUSH TO SET button.

controls.name: Standby horizon cage knob
controls.text: Pulling this knob locks (cages) the gyroscope of the spare horizon so it can be quickly straightened. Turning it without pulling moves the little aircraft symbol up or down.
controls.context: In the game, the hint says to hold the right mouse button and turn the scroll wheel to release (uncage) it. The manual calls this the fast erect knob.

panels.name: Engine and system gauges (main panel) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These dials show how the engine and the plane's systems are doing: engine speed, temperature, oil, fuel use, electricity, hydraulic pressure and the flap and speed brake positions.
panels.context: The pilot glances at them after engine start and regularly in flight. A reading outside the normal range is the first sign of a problem. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: FUEL FLOW RESET button
controls.text: Pressing this button sets the used-fuel counter of the fuel flow indicator back to zero.
controls.context: The pilot resets it after engine start or at the start of a new exercise, so the counter shows the fuel used since then.

panels.name: Warning light buttons and marker lamps (main panel) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These lamps and buttons near the top of the panel get the pilot's attention when something is wrong, and let the pilot say 'understood' or test the lamps.
panels.context: Red lights mean danger now, amber lights mean something needs attention. The warning/caution panel on the right tells which system is meant. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Master warning reset button (FALLO)
controls.text: This red lamp-button lights up when a serious fault occurs. Pressing it switches the lamp and the warning sound off and readies it for the next fault.
controls.context: The warning/caution panel on the right shows which system caused the warning. The label FALLO is Spanish for failure.

controls.name: Master caution reset button (AVISO)
controls.text: This amber lamp-button lights up when a less serious fault occurs. Pressing it switches the lamp off and readies it for the next fault.
controls.context: The warning/caution panel on the right shows what the fault is. The label AVISO is Spanish for caution.

controls.name: FIRE warning light and test button (FUEGO)
controls.text: This red FIRE lamp lights up if the engine is on fire or overheated. Pressing it tests the fire detection circuit.
controls.context: The label FUEGO is Spanish for fire. A FIRE light also shows on the warning/caution panel.

controls.name: INNER MARKER LAMP TEST button
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the lamp for the inner marker beacon, one of the three lamps that flash when the plane flies over a marker beacon.
controls.context: Marker beacons are radio signals sent upward near a runway. The manual says the three lamps are blue, amber and white.

controls.name: MIDDLE MARKER LAMP TEST button
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the lamp for the middle marker beacon.
controls.context: The middle marker is the second of the three marker beacons the plane passes on the way to a runway.

controls.name: OUTER MARKER LAMP TEST button
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the lamp for the outer marker beacon.
controls.context: The outer marker is the first of the three marker beacons on the approach to a runway.

controls.name: Anti-skid status and power button
controls.text: This lamp-button shows the state of the anti-skid system (like ABS in a car, it keeps the wheels from locking when braking) and lets the pilot switch it on or off.
controls.context: The manual lists three looks: connected, failed and disconnected. The pilot checks it before taxiing.

panels.name: Control transfer buttons and gyro controls (main panel) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These buttons hand a radio or the navigation set over to this cockpit. The gyro controls keep the compass and horizon instruments correct.
panels.context: Two pilots share one set of radios. Pressing a transfer button in one cockpit takes control of that equipment for this cockpit. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: UHF control transfer button
controls.text: Pressing this button gives control of the UHF radio to this cockpit. A lit spot shows that this cockpit has control.
controls.context: The UHF radio is the one for talking to other aircraft and the tower on ultra-high frequencies.

controls.name: VHF control transfer button
controls.text: Pressing this button gives control of the VHF radio to this cockpit. A lit spot shows that this cockpit has control.
controls.context: The VHF radio is the second radio, for talking on very-high frequencies.

controls.name: NAV control transfer button
controls.text: Pressing this button gives control of the VOR navigation radio to this cockpit. This includes the fast erect control of the vertical gyro, the TARSYN selector and the HSI knobs.
controls.context: TARSYN is the gyro system that gives the instruments their heading and attitude.

controls.name: VOR/TCN nav selector
controls.text: This push-button chooses which radio source the HSI follows: the VOR beacon or the TACAN beacon.
controls.context: Both pointers of the RMI keep working whichever source is chosen. This button only changes what the HSI shows.

controls.name: Manual gyro correction (dot/cross sync)
controls.text: This switch nudges the heading gyro. The HSI shows a dot and a cross symbol. The pilot presses toward the symbol that is showing until both look equally bright.
controls.context: The gyro drifts slowly with time, so the pilot corrects it now and then in flight. The game offers CROSS and DOT as two commands.

controls.name: Vertical gyro fast erect
controls.text: This switch makes the vertical gyro of the ADI stand upright quickly again, if the picture has become wrong. The ADI shows its OFF flag for about a minute during this.
controls.context: The manual says the gyro also starts and aligns by itself, so this is only for a manual re-start.

controls.name: Gyro mode selector (COMPASS or GYRO)

positions.name: COMPASS
positions.text: The heading is kept in line with the magnetic compass sensor.

positions.name: GYRO
positions.text: The heading comes from the gyroscope alone and may slowly drift.

controls.text: This switch chooses how the HSI gets its heading: from the magnetic compass sensor (COMPASS) or from the free gyroscope alone (GYRO).
controls.context: In compass mode the gyro is corrected by the Earth's magnetic field. In gyro mode the pilot must correct drift by hand.

controls.name: HSI digit brightness knob
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the number displays of the HSI (course and distance) brighter or darker.
controls.context: The manual says the dimmer sits below the standby horizon.

panels.name: UHF radio AN/ARC-164(V) control panel (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This is the control box of the UHF radio, the radio for talking to other aircraft and to the tower. It sets the frequency (the station number) and the volume.
panels.context: The radio covers 225.000 to 339.975 MHz in steps of 25 kHz. The same panel exists in the rear cockpit, and only one cockpit has control at a time. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Function dial (OFF, MAIN, BOTH, ADF)

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The radio is switched off.

positions.name: MAIN
positions.text: The main receiver is on.

positions.name: BOTH
positions.text: The main receiver and the reserve receiver (emergency channel) are on.

positions.name: ADF
positions.text: This position does not work.

controls.text: This dial switches the radio off, on, or on with a second receiver for the emergency channel.
controls.context: The ADF position is not working in this aircraft, says the manual.

controls.name: Frequency mode dial (MANUAL, PRESET, GUARD)

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The frequency is set with the frequency selector knobs.

positions.name: PRESET
positions.text: The radio uses the stored frequency of the chosen preset channel.

positions.name: GUARD
positions.text: The radio tunes to the emergency frequency 243 MHz by itself.

controls.text: This dial chooses how the radio is tuned: by hand with the knobs, by a stored channel number, or to the emergency frequency.
controls.context: The guard frequency, 243 MHz, is the common emergency channel that many aircraft listen on.

controls.name: Frequency selector knobs (5)
controls.text: These five knobs set the frequency digit by digit: 100 MHz, 10 MHz, 1 MHz, 0.1 MHz and 0.025 MHz. The result shows on the display.
controls.context: Frequency is the 'station number' of a radio. Both people must tune the same number to hear each other.

controls.name: Preset channel selector
controls.text: This knob picks one of the stored channels, like a station button on a car radio. The chosen number shows on the preset channel indicator.
controls.context: It is used when the mode dial is on PRESET.

controls.name: UHF preset button
controls.text: The game names this button 'UHF Preset Button'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: It is part of the UHF radio control panel in the game. The manual describes the preset channel selector and indicator, not a separate button.

controls.name: UHF cover
controls.text: The game names this control 'UHF Cover'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: It is part of the UHF radio control panel in the game.

controls.name: Indication mode and test switch
controls.text: This switch is the display mode and test switch of the radio. The game names it 'UHF Digital Display Frequency mode/Test switch'. The manual does not say more about its positions.
controls.context: The manual lists it as the indication mode and test selector. It belongs to the frequency display of the UHF radio.

controls.name: UHF display dimmer
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the frequency display brighter or darker.
controls.context: It helps reading the display in bright sun or at night.

controls.name: T-TONE button
controls.text: Pressing this button makes the radio send a test tone on the tuned frequency.
controls.context: The label in the manual is TONE TEST BUTTON.

controls.name: UHF volume knob
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the radio louder or quieter in the headset.
controls.context: The audio control panel on the right console has a UHF volume button as well.

controls.name: Squelch switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The hiss is cut off when no signal is received.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: All noise from the receiver is heard.

controls.text: Squelch cuts the hiss of the radio when nobody talks. This switch turns the cut-off on or off.
controls.context: With squelch off, the pilot hears all noise from the receiver as well.

panels.name: Red panel light knobs (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These knobs set how bright the red lights are that light up parts of the panels at night. Red light keeps the pilot's eyes used to the dark.
panels.context: They are used for night flying. The manual lists three of them on the main panel and the game has five in total. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: ADJUST RED LIGHT knobs (left centre panel, top centre panel, left console)
controls.text: These three knobs set the brightness of the red light for the left centre panel, the top centre panel and the left console. Turning a knob makes its light brighter or darker.
controls.context: The manual lists three red panel light adjust knobs, numbered 41 to 43, but does not say which is which.

controls.name: ADJUST RED LIGHT knobs (right centre panel, right console)
controls.text: These two knobs set the brightness of the red light for the right centre panel and the right console.
controls.context: They belong to the right half of the cockpit. The manual does not describe them one by one.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: forward left and right panels
areas.text: The rear copies of the gear handle panel and the electrical switches.

panels.name: Forward left panel (landing gear and brakes) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel at the lower left of the instrument panel holds the landing gear handle, the parking brake, the landing lights, the pitot heat and the stall warning switches.
panels.context: The pilot uses it on every take-off and landing: gear up after take-off, gear down before landing, lights for taxiing, brake handle when parking. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Landing gear handle

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The wheels are raised and the gear doors close.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The wheels are lowered and locked.

controls.text: Moving this handle up raises the wheels into the plane. Moving it down lets the wheels come down. A light in the handle flashes red while the wheels are moving.
controls.context: The pilot raises the gear after take-off and lowers it before landing. The two gear handles (front and rear) are joined by a cable. A switch on the main gear stops the handle from going up while the plane stands on the ground.

controls.name: LANDING GEAR OVERRIDE (crash) button
controls.text: This red button, above the gear handle, frees the handle so the wheels can be raised even on the ground.
controls.context: Normally the handle is locked in DOWN while the plane's weight is on the wheels, so the wheels cannot fold by mistake. The manual calls this the crash button.

controls.name: Parking and emergency brake handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle applies the wheel brakes with the emergency hydraulic supply. Pulling it and turning it a quarter turn locks it as the parking brake.
controls.context: The manual says the emergency braking acts on both wheels equally, so the pilot cannot brake one side only with it.

controls.name: PITOT HEAT button
controls.text: This lamp-button heats the pitot tube, the small tube on the nose that measures airspeed, so ice cannot block it. ON shows when the heater works.
controls.context: The angle-of-attack probe is heated at the same time. An amber PITOT HEAT light on the warning panel comes on if the heater circuit fails.

controls.name: LEFT landing light / front cockpit priority switch

positions.name: FRONT
positions.text: The position FRONT named by the game. The manual does not explain it.

positions.name: LAND
positions.text: The landing light is set to LAND.

controls.text: This rear cockpit switch for the left landing light has the positions FRONT and LAND in the game. The game names it 'FWD COCKPIT PRIORITY'.
controls.context: The manual says the outside lights are controlled from the front cockpit. It does not explain the position FRONT of the left switch.

controls.name: RIGHT landing light / front cockpit priority switch

positions.name: FRONT
positions.text: The position FRONT named by the game. The manual does not explain it.

positions.name: LAND
positions.text: The landing light is set to LAND.

controls.text: This rear cockpit switch for the right landing light has the positions FRONT and LAND in the game. The game names it 'FWD COCKPIT PRIORITY'.
controls.context: The manual says the outside lights are controlled from the front cockpit. It does not explain the position FRONT of the right switch.

controls.name: Canopy locking handle

positions.name: FORWARD
positions.text: The canopy is locked.

positions.name: BACK
positions.text: The canopy is unlocked and can be opened.

controls.text: This handle locks the canopy, the glass roof. Moving it forward locks the canopy shut. Moving it back unlocks it so it can be opened.
controls.context: The pilot squeezes the canopy safety catch first, then moves the handle back to open. A red CANOPY light shows on the warning panel if the canopy is not fully locked.

panels.name: Electrical system control panel (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel on the right side switches the plane's electricity: the batteries, the engine generator, the link between the two power lines, the AC converters and the essential supply.
panels.context: The pilot switches it on first when climbing in and it supports everything after that. The manual says the plane has two batteries, one engine-driven generator and two inverters that make alternating current. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Left battery isolation switch
controls.text: This lamp-button shows TEM when the left battery gets too hot. Pressing it cuts the battery off, and then OFF shows. A cover protects the button.
controls.context: The manual says TEM shows at 57 degrees Celsius. A red 70 BAT light shows on the warning panel at 70 degrees.

controls.name: Right battery isolation switch
controls.text: This lamp-button does the same for the right battery: TEM warns of overheat, pressing it isolates the battery, and OFF then shows. A cover protects the button.
controls.context: Each battery has its own switch, so one hot battery can be cut off while the other keeps working.

controls.name: ESS BUS transfer switch
controls.text: This lamp-button chooses which power line feeds the essential bus, the line that keeps the most important equipment alive. ON shows when it is fed from the secondary bus. A cover protects the button.
controls.context: Normally the essential bus is fed from the primary bus. If the generator or the batteries fail, the pilot can switch it to the other line.

controls.name: Warning/caution panel BRIGHT/DIM switch

positions.name: BRIGHT
positions.text: The panel lights are bright.

positions.name: DIM
positions.text: The panel lights are dimmed.

controls.text: This switch sets how bright the lights of the warning/caution panel are: bright for daytime, dim for night.
controls.context: It has the two positions BRIGHT and DIM.

controls.name: Lamp test switch (warning/caution panel)
controls.text: Holding this spring-loaded switch on TEST lights all the lamps of the warning/caution panel and sounds the warning tones. This shows that the lamps and sounds work.
controls.context: The pilot does the test after switching on the electricity.

panels.name: Air vent and standby compass (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These are small items in the right half of the front cockpit: a fresh-air knob and the standby compass with its lamp.
panels.context: They are not needed for flying procedures, but they are part of the cockpit. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: AIR VENT knob
controls.text: Turning this knob changes how much air blows from the vent into the cockpit.
controls.context: The manual lists an air blower control on the main panel. The game names this knob AIR VENT.

panels.name: Rear cockpit extras (instructor seat)
panels.text: These controls exist only in the rear cockpit, where the instructor sits: the blackout hood for instrument training, the flight director dimmer and seat levers.
panels.context: The manual says the rear cockpit can be fitted with blackout curtains for instrument flight training, and that the rear seat has its own lever and switch copies.

controls.name: FD Bright/Dim switch

positions.name: Bright
positions.text: The lamps are bright.

positions.name: Dim
positions.text: The lamps are dimmed.

controls.text: This switch sets how bright the flight director annunciator lamps in the rear cockpit are.
controls.context: The rear annunciator repeats the modes chosen with the buttons in the front cockpit.

controls.name: Ejection seat priority lever

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The lever is ON, as named by the game.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The lever is OFF, as named by the game.

controls.text: The game names this lever 'Ejection Seat Priority Lever'. It has the positions ON and OFF. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: It is part of the rear ejection seat controls of the game.

controls.name: Oxygen pressure warning switch (BOTH or FRONT)

positions.name: BOTH
positions.text: The position BOTH named by the game.

positions.name: FRONT
positions.text: The position FRONT named by the game.

controls.text: The game names this switch 'Oxygen pressure warning switch' with the positions BOTH and FRONT. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: It belongs to the oxygen controls of the rear right console.

controls.name: Oxygen regulator control (100% or AIRMIX)

positions.text: Pure oxygen.

positions.name: AIRMIX
positions.text: Oxygen mixed with cabin air.

controls.text: This control on the rear seat sets what the instructor breathes: 100% means pure oxygen, AIRMIX means oxygen mixed with cabin air.
controls.context: The game names it 'Oxygen Regulator - 100%/AIRMIX'. The manual does not describe the regulator control itself.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: pedestal and ejection seat
areas.text: The rear copies of the heading and course knobs, the IFF box and the ejection seat handles.

panels.name: HSI course and heading knobs (forward lower panel) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These two knobs on the lower panel set the course and the heading marks on the HSI compass dial.
panels.context: The pilot sets the wanted heading or the radio course here before using the flight director. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Course knob (HSI course selector)
controls.text: Turning this knob moves the yellow course arrow around the HSI dial. This chooses the radio line or runway line the pilot wants to follow. The number shows in the course window.
controls.context: The game offers the commands course knob increase and decrease. The manual calls this the remote course knob.

controls.name: Heading knob (HSI heading selector)
controls.text: Turning this knob moves the orange heading marker (the heading bug) around the HSI dial. This chooses the direction the pilot wants to fly.
controls.context: The flight director's HDG mode steers toward this marker. The game offers heading knob increase and decrease.

controls.name: Rudder pedal adjustment handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle lets the pilot slide the rudder pedals forward or back to suit the length of the legs. Releasing the handle locks the pedals.
controls.context: In the game the left mouse button pulls the handle and the right mouse button moves the pedals.

panels.name: Ejection seat handles (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These are the handles of the ejection seat, the seat that shoots the pilot out of the plane in an emergency. They also hold the safety parts that make the seat safe on the ground.
panels.context: The manual says the seat is a Martin-Baker Mk-10 that works from zero speed and zero height. Red safety pins make it safe on the ground and must be removed before flight. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Ejection handle (seat firing handle)

positions.name: PULL
positions.text: The seat is fired.

positions.name: PUSH
positions.text: The handle is put back.

controls.text: Pulling this handle fires the ejection seat. The seat and pilot leave the plane. It is between the pilot's legs on the front of the seat.
controls.context: It is the last resort. In the game the handle has the commands PULL and PUSH.

controls.name: Ejection handle safety (pin)
controls.text: This safety pin makes the ejection handle safe on the ground. It must be removed before flight.
controls.context: The game names it 'EJECTION HANDLE SAFETY'. The manual speaks of red safety pins that must be removed before flight.

controls.name: MANUAL SEPARATION handle
controls.text: The name of this handle says it separates the pilot from the seat by hand. The manual lists it as part of the ejection seat and does not explain it further.
controls.context: It is part of the seat's emergency equipment.

controls.name: SHOW/HIDE FLIGHT STICK
controls.text: This control shows or hides the flight stick in the 3D cockpit.
controls.context: It is a viewing option of the game. It does not change how the plane flies.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: left console
areas.text: The rear copies of the engine start switches, the fuel panel, the power lever with the flap lever, the emergency panel and the secondary circuit breaker panel.

panels.name: Engine control panel (start switches) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel on the left console starts the jet engine. It has the start and ignition switches, a switch for outside power, a computer button and an anti-ice button.
panels.context: The manual says every cockpit has such a panel, but the engine can be started only from the front cockpit. After the start the engine runs by itself. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: STARTER MODE selector (NORMAL, CRANK)

positions.name: Normal
positions.text: The automatic start sequence is ready. The engine starts when the ignition switch is held to START.

positions.name: Crank
positions.text: The engine is only turned by the starter, with no start sequence. This clears fuel left in the combustion chamber.

controls.text: This switch chooses between a normal engine start and only spinning the engine without fuel. Spinning without fuel clears left-over fuel after a failed start.
controls.context: The manual calls it the START switch, marked NORMAL and VENTILACION (CRANK).

controls.name: CONTINUOUS IGNITION/START switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The igniters are off.

positions.name: START
positions.text: The igniters and the starter-generator are energised (hold for about 2 seconds).

positions.name: CONTINUOUS
positions.text: Only the igniters are on, to keep the engine lit.

controls.text: This switch lights the engine. Holding it to START for about 2 seconds starts the igniters and the starter. In CONT IGN only the igniters run, as a safety against the engine going out.
controls.context: The manual says to use continuous ignition for take-off, landing, icing, heavy turbulence and thunderstorms. The yellow ignition light is on while the igniters work.

controls.name: ENGINE START (ignition) light test
controls.text: This yellow light shows when the igniters are on. Pressing it tests the bulb.
controls.context: The manual calls it the ignition light, a press-to-test light next to the ignition switch.

controls.name: ABORT start switch

positions.name: NEUTRAL
positions.text: The start continues normally.

positions.name: ABORT
positions.text: The starter-generator is switched off while the switch is held.

controls.text: Holding this switch to ABORT switches the starter off, to stop a start that goes wrong. It springs back when released.
controls.context: The manual says it is used before the starter drops out by itself at 50 percent N2. It is also used for a start with the engine computer out of order.

controls.name: COMPUTER button (engine computer)
controls.text: This lamp-button switches the engine computer between automatic mode (the light stays out) and manual mode (MAN lights amber). The engine computer helps look after the fuel supply of the engine.
controls.context: If the computer fails, an amber COMPUT. light comes on in the warning panel.

controls.name: ANTI-ICE button (engine)
controls.text: This lamp-button turns the engine anti-ice on. Warm air from the engine then keeps ice from forming at the engine inlet. ON shows when it is working.
controls.context: The manual says ice can form when the air is at or below 10 degrees Celsius and there is visible moisture.

controls.name: GPU (ground power) button
controls.text: This lamp-button connects an outside power cart (GPU) to the plane's electrical system. GPU shows green when a cart is plugged in and ready, and ON shows when its power is connected.
controls.context: The manual says the batteries and the generator disconnect by themselves while the outside power is connected.

panels.name: Fuel control panel (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel on the left console controls how fuel moves from the wing tanks to the main tank and shows how much fuel is left.
panels.context: The plane has four tanks: one in the fuselage, one in the centre wing and one in each outer wing. The engine always draws from the fuselage tank. The wing tanks feed it through pumps. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Fuel transfer pump switch, left

positions.name: AUT
positions.text: The pump runs until all the fuel of this tank has been moved. The game spells it ANT here.

positions.name: MAN
positions.text: The pump runs until the switch is set to OFF. The manual says to use this only in abnormal cases, so the pump does not run dry.

controls.text: This switch controls the transfer pump of the left outer wing tank. The pump moves fuel from that tank into the fuselage tank.
controls.context: The manual says to use up the outer wing tanks first, then the centre tank. In the rear cockpit the game names the switch 'Fuel Transfer .../Fwd Cockpit Priority' and offers only AUT and MAN. The manual does not explain the extra words.

controls.name: Fuel transfer pump switch, centre 1

positions.name: AUT
positions.text: The pump runs until all the fuel of this tank has been moved. The game spells it ANT here.

positions.name: MAN
positions.text: The pump runs until the switch is set to OFF.

controls.text: This switch controls the first of two transfer pumps in the centre wing tank.
controls.context: The centre tank has two pumps. Together with the left and right outer tank pumps there are four transfer pumps. In the rear cockpit the game names the switch 'Fuel Transfer .../Fwd Cockpit Priority' and offers only AUT and MAN. The manual does not explain the extra words.

controls.name: Fuel transfer pump switch, centre 2

positions.name: AUT
positions.text: The pump runs until all the fuel of this tank has been moved. The game spells it ANT here.

positions.name: MAN
positions.text: The pump runs until the switch is set to OFF.

controls.text: This switch controls the second transfer pump in the centre wing tank.
controls.context: A second pump in the same tank keeps fuel moving if the first one fails. In the rear cockpit the game names the switch 'Fuel Transfer .../Fwd Cockpit Priority' and offers only AUT and MAN. The manual does not explain the extra words.

controls.name: Fuel transfer pump switch, right

positions.name: AUT
positions.text: The pump runs until all the fuel of this tank has been moved. The game spells it ANT here.

positions.name: MAN
positions.text: The pump runs until the switch is set to OFF.

controls.text: This switch controls the transfer pump of the right outer wing tank.
controls.context: It works like the left switch. Check valves stop fuel from flowing from one wing tank to another. In the rear cockpit the game names the switch 'Fuel Transfer .../Fwd Cockpit Priority' and offers only AUT and MAN. The manual does not explain the extra words.

controls.name: Fuselage tank pump (boost pump) switch
controls.text: This guarded lamp-button controls the boost pump, a pump in the fuselage tank that pushes fuel to the engine. The button is dark while the pump works. Pressing it stops the pump and OFF lights up. A cover protects the button.
controls.context: The manual says the pump is submerged in the engine feed cell of the fuselage tank.

controls.name: Engine fuel valve (shut-off) switch
controls.text: This guarded lamp-button controls the shut-off valve between the fuselage tank and the engine. OFF lights up when the valve is closed. A cover protects the button.
controls.context: An amber FUEL VALVE light on the warning panel comes on whenever the valve is not fully open.

controls.name: Fuel quantity selector (centre wing tank quantity)
controls.text: This lamp-button chooses what the fuel quantity dial shows: only the fuselage tank (FUS lights amber) or the fuselage tank plus the centre wing tank.
controls.context: The manual says that without transfer pressure the dial always shows the fuselage tank only.

panels.name: Power lever quadrant, flap lever and gear warning silence (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The power lever, the flap lever and a silence button are mounted together on the left console. The power lever works the engine, the flap lever the flaps.
panels.context: The manual says the front power lever has a friction lock. Both cockpits have a lever, joined by a flexible link. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Power lever idle/stop gate (THROTTLE IDLE DETENT)

positions.name: Idle
positions.text: The power lever is at idle.

positions.name: Stop
positions.text: The power lever is at STOP and the fuel is cut off.

controls.text: This is the gate at the idle end of the power lever travel. The pilot lifts the lever to pass the gate from IDLE to STOP. At STOP the fuel to the engine is cut.
controls.context: The gate protects against shutting the fuel off by accident while slowing down. The game offers the positions Idle, Stop and a two-position idle/stop switch.

controls.name: Landing gear warning silence button
controls.text: Pressing this button silences the warning tone that sounds when the wheels are up and the engine power is low.
controls.context: The manual says the tone sounds when a wheel is not down and locked below 6500 feet and 75 percent N1. The amber GEAR light stays on as long as this is true.

controls.name: Flap lever (FLAP POSITION SELECTOR)

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The flaps are fully retracted.

positions.name: TAKEOFF
positions.text: The flaps are set to 10 degrees.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The flaps are set to 30 degrees.

controls.text: This lever sets the flaps, the parts of the wing that slide out to give more lift at low speed. It has three marked positions: UP, TAKEOFF (10 degrees) and DOWN (30 degrees).
controls.context: The pilot sets TAKEOFF for take-off and DOWN for landing. The three windows on the instrument panel show where the flaps are.

panels.name: Emergency panel (left console) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel holds backup controls for failures of the trim, the speed brake and the ailerons, plus the emergency landing gear handle and the seat height switch.
panels.context: These controls are normally left alone. Several have guards or covers so they cannot be moved by accident. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Emergency elevator trim switch (with guard)

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The pitch trim moves to nose up.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: No emergency trim. The trim works from the stick switch.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The pitch trim moves to nose down.

controls.text: This switch trims the nose up or down if the trim switch on the stick fails. A guard must be turned aside first. Trim means a steady push that keeps the plane flying straight without holding the stick.
controls.context: The manual says that with the guard open the trim switches on the stick and the speed brake are cut out.

controls.name: PITCH TRIM DISC lamp test
controls.text: This light comes on when the emergency trim switch drives the stabilizer. Pressing it tests the bulb.
controls.context: The manual calls it the press-to-test light next to the emergency trim switch.

controls.name: EMERGENCY AIR BRAKE RETRACT button
controls.text: Pressing this guarded button lets the speed brake close partly if the hydraulics fail, because the wind then pushes it in.
controls.context: The manual says this reduces the large drag that the fully open brake makes.

controls.name: AILERON HYD OVERRIDE (servo-actuator cutout) with cover
controls.text: This guarded button cuts the hydraulic help from the ailerons, so a pilot can practise flying with heavy controls. MAN lights when it is on.
controls.context: The manual says this function is not simulated in DCS: C-101.

controls.name: SEAT HEIGHT ADJUSTMENT switch
controls.text: This switch moves the ejection seat up or down, to suit the pilot's height.
controls.context: The manual says the seat elevation switch has two positions, UP and DOWN, that show the direction of travel.

controls.name: EMERGENCY LANDING GEAR EXTENSION handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle lowers the wheels with a bottle of nitrogen gas if the normal system fails. It works whatever position the gear handle is in.
controls.context: The manual says it can be used only once. After the gear has been lowered this way, it cannot be raised by hydraulics again. The label is EMERG. TREN.

panels.name: Seat harness handle and canopy safety catch (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These two controls are at the left side of the seat: the shoulder harness handle and the catch that secures the canopy.
panels.context: They are used when strapping in and when opening or closing the canopy. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: SHOULDER HARNESS CONTROL HANDLE
controls.text: The game names this handle 'SHOULDER HARNESS CONTROL HANDLE'. The manual does not describe it. A shoulder harness is the belt that holds the pilot in the seat.
controls.context: It is one of the seat controls of the game's cockpit.

controls.name: Canopy safety catch
controls.text: Squeezing this catch lets the pilot open the canopy. To close and lock it, the pilot grabs the catch first, closes the canopy and then moves the locking handle forward.
controls.context: The manual describes the canopy opening to the right.

panels.context: The manual says most electrical circuits are protected by pop-out thermal breakers. The main panel is on the front left console and a secondary panel on the rear left console covers circuits of the rear cockpit only.
