areas.name: Rear cockpit: right console
areas.text: The rear copies of the lights, audio panel, radios, air conditioning and oxygen controls.

panels.name: Illumination panel (cockpit and outside lights) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel on the right console switches the lights: the cockpit lights for night flying and the lights on the outside of the plane.
panels.context: The manual says the cockpit lights are controlled in each cockpit, while the outside lights are controlled from the front cockpit only. The rear cockpit has its own lamps for the cabin. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: INSTRUMENT LIGHTING knob
controls.text: Turning this knob switches on the lights inside the instruments and sets how bright they are.
controls.context: The manual calls it the integral instrument light switch.

controls.name: CONSOLE INTEGRAL LIGHTING knob
controls.text: Turning this knob switches on the lights of the console panels (the side panels) and sets their brightness.
controls.context: The manual calls it the console lights switch.

controls.name: STORM LIGHTS switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The storm lights are on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The storm lights are off.

controls.text: This switch turns on the storm lights. These are very bright white lights that light the whole cockpit, so lightning flashes do not blind the pilot.
controls.context: The manual says there are two storm lights in each cockpit.

controls.name: RED FLOOD LIGHTING switch (auxiliary lights)

positions.name: BRIGHT
positions.text: The lights are on at full brightness. The manual calls this BRILLO.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The lights are off.

positions.name: TENUE
positions.text: The lights are on but dimmed. The manual calls this TENUE (DIM).

controls.text: This switch turns on the red auxiliary lights that gently light the cockpit at night, with two levels of brightness.
controls.context: The manual says the red auxiliary lights have the positions BRILLO (bright), OFF and TENUE (dim). Red light keeps the eyes used to the dark.

panels.name: Audio control panel (INT) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel is the volume and radio mixer for the pilot's headset. It switches on the radios the pilot wants to hear and sets how loud each one is. It also controls the intercom between the two crew members.
panels.context: The manual calls it the audio control system AN/AIC-18. It lets each pilot listen to any navigation station and to any radio on his own. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Receiver on/volume buttons (UHF, VHF, TCN, VOR, MK)
controls.text: Each of these five buttons switches one receiver into the headset and sets its volume. Pulling the button out turns the receiver on. Turning it sets the volume.
controls.context: UHF and VHF are the two radios, TCN is TACAN, VOR is the VOR receiver and MK is the marker beacon receiver. Pulling out the TACAN or VOR button lets the pilot hear the station's identification tone.

controls.name: INT button (interphone on/volume)
controls.text: Pulling this button out and turning it sets the volume of the interphone, the intercom between the two crew members.
controls.context: To talk on the interphone, the pilot also sets the selector switch to INT and presses the push-to-talk switch.

controls.name: HM button (hot mic mode on/volume)
controls.text: Pulling this button out switches on the hot microphone mode. In this mode the crew can talk to each other without pressing a button.
controls.context: The manual says the HOT MIC TALK button has to be pulled out too, and this button is then turned to the volume wanted.

controls.name: HOT MIC TALK button
controls.text: Pulling this button out switches the microphone on for the hot microphone mode.
controls.context: The game labels it '(HOT MIC) TALK CIRCUIT BREAKER'. The manual calls it the HOT MIC TALK button.

controls.name: General volume knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the overall volume in the headset.
controls.context: The manual calls it the general volume knob, number 11 of the audio panel.

controls.name: Selector switch
controls.text: This switch chooses which system the pilot talks to when pressing the push-to-talk switch: for example the interphone (INT) or one of the radios.
controls.context: The manual says the selector must be at INT for talking on the interphone.

controls.name: CALL button
controls.text: Pressing this button is an emergency call between the two cockpits. It overrides the interphone and hot microphone modes.
controls.context: The manual calls it an emergency mode.

panels.name: VHF radio AN/ARC-134 control panel (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This is the control box of the VHF radio, the second radio of the plane. It sets the frequency and the volume.
panels.context: The manual says the radio covers 116.000 to 149.975 MHz in steps of 25 kHz. Both cockpits have a panel, and only one has control at a time. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: POWER switch (VHF)
controls.text: This switch is the power switch of the VHF radio. It turns the radio on or off.
controls.context: The manual lists a power switch, number 1 in its figure. The game does not list the positions.

controls.name: DISPLAY TEST button (VHF)
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the number display of the VHF radio.
controls.context: The manual calls it the digits test.

controls.name: Frequency selector knobs (4)
controls.text: These four knobs set the frequency digit by digit: 10 MHz, 1 MHz, 0.1 MHz and 25 kHz steps. The number shows on the display.
controls.context: The frequency is the 'station number' of the radio. Both people must tune the same number to hear each other.

controls.name: VHF volume and brightness knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the display brightness and the radio volume.
controls.context: The manual calls it the dimmer/volume knob.

panels.name: VOR/ILS radio AN/ARN-127 control panel (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This is the control box of the VOR and ILS receiver. It tunes the radio beacons (VOR) and the runway beams (ILS) that guide the plane. A small test and dimmer panel sits next to it.
panels.context: The manual says the receiver covers 108.00 to 117.95 MHz in 50 kHz steps. It also receives the marker beacons. The signal shows on the HSI, ADI and RMI. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: VOR frequency selector knobs (3)
controls.text: These three knobs tune the VOR frequency: the first in 1 MHz steps (108 to 117), the second in 0.1 MHz steps and the third in 50 kHz steps.
controls.context: A VOR is a ground beacon that tells the pilot the direction to it. The pilot reads the direction on the RMI and the HSI.

controls.name: NAV VOL knob (VOR off/volume)
controls.text: Turning this knob switches the VOR receiver on and sets its volume.
controls.context: The manual calls it the OFF/VOLUME knob.

controls.name: TEST VOR/MKR button
controls.text: Pressing this button runs the VOR test, and the three marker beacon lamps light up.
controls.context: The manual calls it the VOR/MARKERS TEST button.

controls.name: TEST VHF NAV DIGITS button
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the number display of the VOR panel.
controls.context: The manual calls it the digits test.

controls.name: DIMMER knob (VOR)
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the display of the VOR panel brighter or darker.
controls.context: It helps reading the display at night.

panels.name: Oxygen panel and valve lever (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This part of the right console holds the controls and gauges for the pilot's breathing oxygen.
panels.context: At high altitude the air is too thin to breathe, so the pilot breathes oxygen from two bottles in the nose of the plane. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: OXYGEN SUPPLY valve lever

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The oxygen valve is open.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The oxygen valve is closed.

controls.text: This lever opens or closes the oxygen valve of this cockpit.
controls.context: The lever is marked A (open) and C (close). The pilot opens it before flight.

panels.name: Other right console controls (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These are the remaining controls on the right side of the cockpit: the canopy detachment handle and the storage box.
panels.context: None of them is used in a normal flight. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: CANOPY EMERGENCY JETTISON handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle lets the canopy come completely off for an emergency exit or for maintenance.
controls.context: The manual calls it the interior canopy detachment handle and says there is one on the right side of each cockpit.

controls.name: STORAGE BOX COVER
controls.text: The game names this control 'STORAGE BOX COVER'. It opens the cover of a storage box. The manual only mentions a map case on the right console.
controls.context: It is a clickable part of the game's cockpit.
